rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Each turn 2.1 Take a standard turn 2.2 Pass 3 Special rounds 4 End Game Scoring Overview Each player has a number of Servant meeples, a set of Improvement tiles in front of them (representing areas of their estate's house and grounds), and a hand of Gentry cards. They also have a Reputation value, starting at 1.1; an amount of Money starting at £0; and a number of Objective Cards (some of which will be discarded as the game progresses). Your Servant meeples are: Meeple Name Effect Butler Supports prestigious events and can hire new servants. Valet Supports male guests. Lady's Maid Supports female guests. Housekeeper Supports dining events and may also serve as a Lady's Maid . Footman Supports outdoor events. Underbutler Can serve as a Butler , Valet or Footman . With Upstairs Downstairs expansion: Cook Increases the family’s reputation by one when used. Permits guests with prestige ratings 1 or 2 levels above family’s rep to attend activity. Hall Boy Duties as Butler when required for a gentry guest, even if Butler is present. May be used on any gentry card to increase the monetary favour by + £100. Head Housemaid Duties as Housekeeper for required female gentry guest (card), even if present, but may not screen guests acting in this capacity. On invite card or tile, may look at 1 additional (“see 2/keep 1” becomes “see 3/keep 1” ; “5/2” etc.). Useful Man Can perform various useful tasks: • Play onto Village Fair to increase by +£200; • Play onto a tile when buying to reduce cost by -£100; • Play onto an improvement tile to temporarily decrease its prestige rating by 1; • Remove the Useful Man from the game to refresh the builders' market; • Remove the Useful Man from the game to locate any non-monument tile and place it in the £800 place in the market. (The tile in the £300 space is returned to the bag and the others moved to the left.) The game consists of players taking turns to host events at locations on their estate: each event requires a number of Servants to attend, and a number of Gentry to be played from the hand as guests to it. The outcome of an event will be a gain (or loss) of Reputation and/or Money, and/or the acquisition of new Gentry cards. After hosting an event, you may optionally buy one Improvement from the Builder's Market. When your hand is running low, you can pass your turn to pick your discard pile back up - optionally taking either £200 or refreshing the Builder's Market. Each turn On your turn you can either: Take a standard turn A standard turn consists of the following steps: 1. Rotate service : Move all your Servants one box to the right. (Only those in the "Available Service" box will be available for use on your turn.) 2. Host activity : Choose tile from your estate to use this turn. Its bottom-left number must be equal to or lower than your family's Reputation. 3. Invite guests : Play a number of Gentry cards from your hand that match the event. 4. Provide service : Expend Servants to satisfy the event's Estate tile and Gentry cards. (If you do not have sufficient servants, you must go back and choose a different Estate/Gentry combination, or give up and pass your turn.) 5. Enjoy favours given by the event tile and the played gentry cards. These are all compulsory, with the exception of "Dismissing". 6. Optionally buy an Improvement tile from Builders' Market 7. Clean up Pass When you choose to pass: • All of your servants move into the "available" box • You take your discard pile of Gentry cards back into your hand • You may either: • Collect £200 • Refresh the Builders' Market • Hire Servants using the Butler's Room (if using the Upstairs Downstairs expansion) • You may optionally buy from the Builders' Market Special Actions At any time: • Spend 2 Reputation to gain £100 • Spend 3 Reputation to refresh 1 Servant • Spend 4 Reputation to refresh the Builders' Market Special rounds Event Regular Game Extended Game Effect Village Fair Rounds 3 and 9 Rounds 4, 9 and 16 Players who have flipped the Study tile receive £300 and 2 Reputation at the starts of these rounds. Courtship Rounds 4, 8, 12 and 16 Rounds 5, 10, 15 and 20 No regular turns are taken: instead, whoever has the highest score for that courtship's current Theme colour (shown by the most recent upturned card at the top of the board) may take either the Charles or Elizabeth Fairchild card into their hand, and draw a Victory Point Card. The final Courtship round is scored on the total for all four Theme colours, rather than just the fourth. (If a colour appears multiple times, it is counted multiple times.) Builder's Holiday Round 11 Round 13 Players may buy any number of Improvement tiles during this round. National Holiday Round 14 Round 11 Player Reputation does not limit actions this round. Players may host any event and invite any guest, irrespective of their Reputation. End Game Scoring Add up: • Improvement Tile VP • Gentry Card VP • Objective Card VP • Service VP: 2 VP per servant • Wealth VP: 1 VP per £200 • VP Cards • Reputation VP Reputation Level VP 1 1 2 3 3 6 4 10 5 15 6 21 7* 28 8 36 Max 45 *Maximum in Standard Play

[Rating: 1/10] :star::nostar::nostar::nostar::nostar:  Literally one of the most boring and shallow games I have played this year. I was initially drawn to the theme and enjoyed it during the first round or so. But the game went on, lost the theme amidst the calculation of the calculable solutions. At that point, it became a boring and soulless game that is not so different from the usual mediocrity that are being released today.

[Rating: 1/10] Heads down low interaction game that goes way too long.  I witnessed a 3+ hour game which is crazy, not enough here for that! + Loved the theme, wish the game lived up to it. Nice art and components – Straight forward puzzle, feel I've grasped it after one game – Objective random draw and early discards were far too random. I'd probably come up with a variant to fix this so you could work on longer range goals through the entire game – Interaction was super low

[Rating: 1/10] There was absolutely nothing I liked about this game. Nothing. It was so dull and boring. The cards are ugly and the game drags on. Just why is it so high on BGG?

[Rating: 1/10] A game I almost like because it really leans into its theme. I like building the rooms with silly names. But the worker placement is too limiting, half the turns you just don't do much. And there's the reputation requirements (which I didn't notice the first time playing) and that makes a lot of things a chore to do, rather than outwitting the other players.

[Rating: 1/10] So boring. Feels like it takes forever to play. Unreadable cards and tiles.  The game is mostly sitting around watching other players take their turn with no interaction and very little actual strategy. The only real strategy is figuring out how to never be asked to play this again.   If I had unfortunately bought this I would have thrown it in the trash rather than giving it away.  I don't think I've ever hated playing a game this much.

[Rating: 1/10] Way too random, also really dull unless you role play the game which if everyone one does that makes the game way too long for what it is.

[Rating: 1/10] Tragically multiplayer-solitaire euro, redeemed for 15 minutes by its presentation and theme and then regressing for 3 hours into a (basically random) attempt of tactically optimising turns and making points head-down looking at the table… booooring! Ideal for socially challenged types who abhor any interaction, storytelling or creativity in games… and there would be a way to role-play this a tiny bit... but nobody wanted to even try at my table... avoid… especially with 6 players... who would want to inflict that level of downtime on their friends?!?

[Rating: 1.2/10] I hate games that are totally luck driven, full of randomness and at the same time force you to constantly develop plans, strategies which are put into trash every single time its time for you to play. I hate even more games who fool you into being something they are not, promising something that they tragically not deliver.  Among many many games I have played there are very few games who perfectly fulfill all those criteria. Obsession is one of the top 3 of those on the "hated list". You then have to spend a worker in the color matching the box on the tile. The tile then often lets you play some number of cards from your hand. The cards often cost additional workers of varied colors, and then the cards also produce their benefits. [Rating: 2/10] To much randomness and multiplayer solitaire for my tastes. There also seems to be economic snowball effects and runaway leader problems, which is particulary problematic since so much depends on luck (more skilled players may disagree of course).   The theme is original and well implemented, and components are good quality.  Rated for first printing/KS.
